references.text: Moses instructs Aaron to take the censer with incense and hurry to the congregation to make atonement for them, as the Lord's wrath has broken out.
Aaron stood between the dead and the living, and the plague stopped - this describes the result of Aaron's action with the incense.
Incense is used in the atonement ritual on the Day of Atonement, showing the role of incense in making atonement for the people.
Aaron was to burn fragrant incense on the altar every morning and evening, illustrating the priest's role with the incense offering.
Phinehas made atonement for the Israelites by acting quickly, just as Aaron ran to stop the plague.
Christ as High Priest makes atonement for the people's sins, a parallel to Aaron's act of atonement to stop the plague.
Incense rises before God's face together with the prayers of the saints, showing the symbolic meaning of incense in intercession.
